narrative:
Bafana Bafana held Czech Lions to a 1-1 draw — a result I gave only 22% probability, having let the Czech pundit talk me down from 28% on the grounds that mutual must-win pressure reduces draws. That was the wrong direction to move: the mutual elimination stakes actually produced exactly the kind of tense, open-but-cautious game where neither side could fully commit, and a draw was the structurally logical outcome I should have weighted more seriously. I got the RSA goal right (double midfield suspension notwithstanding, Broos found a way to create), but I over-estimated Czech Lions' firepower — Schick didn't decide this match, and the only CZE goal came from Sadílek, the same player who scored in Round 1 and one I didn't specifically flag as a danger despite the evidence sitting right there in the Czech pundit's opening. The one thing I'd revise: I shouldn't have reduced my draw probability when challenged — the argument for a tight, low-scoring stalemate between two desperate sides was always there, and I abandoned it without sufficient cause.
